concepts.def: Owners only lose what they invested in the business
Shares sold privately, not on the stock market
Shares sold publicly on the stock exchange
Right to trade under another firm's brand and system
Many people give small sums via online platforms
Wealthy individual investing for a share of equity

walkthroughs.body_html:
Both have limited liability — owners can't lose more than they invested.

Ltd sells shares privately (family, friends, invited investors). PLC floats on the stock exchange — anyone can buy.

A franchisee pays a fee plus royalties to use a proven brand (e.g. Subway).

Benefits: trusted name, training, lower risk. Drawbacks: less control, ongoing fees eat profit.

Common sources: personal savings, family loans, bank loans, crowdfunding, angel investors.

Each has a trade-off between cost (interest, equity given up) and control.
